summary: The Heinrich Böll Foundation funds international students for a master's or PhD at a state-recognised German university: €992 a month for a master's or €1,500 for a PhD, plus health insurance and up to €10,000 a year towards tuition. It looks for good grades, civic commitment and German at B2 level, and gives priority to applicants from DAC countries. The next round runs from 15 January to 1 March 2027.
meta_title: Heinrich Böll scholarship for international students: €992 a month
meta_description: Böll Foundation scholarships for a master's or PhD in Germany: €992 or €1,500 a month, insurance and tuition help. Next round 15 Jan to 1 Mar 2027.
covers: Master's: a base scholarship of €992 a month, plus a health insurance allowance of up to €100.
PhD: a base scholarship of €1,500 a month, plus up to €200 a month for health insurance.
Optional: up to €10,000 a year towards tuition fees in Germany, German course fees, €38 a month in fringe benefits, and family and child allowances.
No extra money for study periods abroad, and other income is offset against the payment.
eligibility: International students who finished their first degree abroad and are about to start a master's in Germany, or graduates starting a PhD in Germany.
A full-time programme at a state-recognised German university; master's programmes must last at least four semesters.
German at B2 or DSH II level, even for a programme taught in English.
Priority for applicants from DAC countries who do not yet live in Germany.
Support for the foundation's goals of a just, democratic and ecological world, and an interest in politics.
how_to_apply: Read the requirements and the info sheet for your level on the foundation's applying page.
Register on the online portal, which opens six weeks before the deadline, and fill in the form with Adobe Acrobat Reader.
Upload proof of German, your certificates with certified translations, an expert report from a professor and a reference for your civic engagement.
Submit between 15 January and 1 March 2027 for the spring round. You can submit as soon as your documents are complete.
watch_out: The foundation's applying page adds: "Note for Master's students: Starting March 1, 2027, we will only accept applications for first-cycle programs." Other parts of its site still invite master's applicants, so ask studienwerk@boell.de before relying on the March 2027 round for a master's.
Application documents should be in German; references, expert opinions and translations may be in English.
Proof of enrolment or admission at a German university is needed by the third selection stage at the latest.
costs: Up to €10,000 a year if approved
documents: Proof of German at B2 or DSH II level.
Your school-leaving and bachelor's certificates, each certified translation in one file with its original.
An expert report on the foundation's template from a professor or a researcher with a PhD.
A reference for your civic engagement on the foundation's form.
Proof of enrolment or admission at a German university, by the third selection stage at the latest.

faq.q: How much does the Heinrich Böll scholarship pay international students?
faq.a: €992 a month for a master's or €1,500 for a PhD, plus a health insurance allowance and, if approved, up to €10,000 a year towards tuition in Germany.

faq.q: Do I need to speak German for the Böll scholarship?
faq.a: Yes. The foundation requires German at B2 or DSH II level, even for programmes taught in English.

faq.q: When is the next Böll deadline?
faq.a: The spring 2027 round is open from 15 January to 1 March 2027. The round after that closes on 1 September 2027.
